title: Frame a clinic access problem
casePrompt: CedarCare's outpatient clinics report that average appointment wait time increased from 8 to 13 days while patient visits grew. The COO wants to improve access without reducing care quality.

responseCycle.prompt: Restate the decision CedarCare needs to make, including the outcome and guardrail that matter.
guidance: Separate the access outcome from the constraint on care quality.

criteria.label: Frames the operational decision, not just the symptom
Names appointment wait time as the target outcome
Preserves care quality as a decision guardrail

comparison.title: One focused restatement
comparison.text: I want to determine what is driving CedarCare's longer appointment waits and which operational changes can restore timely access without weakening care quality.

questionOptions.label: How is appointment wait time measured, and for which visit types?
questionOptions.response: It is calendar days from a patient's request to the earliest offered appointment, across new and follow-up visits.

questionOptions.label: Is the increase broad or concentrated by clinic, specialty, or time period?
questionOptions.response: Most of the deterioration is concentrated in primary-care clinics during the last six months.

questionOptions.label: Which quality or staffing constraints cannot be compromised?
questionOptions.response: The COO will not shorten visits below clinical guidelines or rely on sustained clinician overtime.

questionOptions.label: When were clinic lobbies last repainted?
questionOptions.response: Lobby appearance is not linked to appointment availability.

questionOptions.label: Can we interview every patient before analyzing operations?
questionOptions.response: That would delay the decision and is not needed for the initial capacity diagnosis.

title: Clarify a subscriber-retention decision
casePrompt: StreamWave's reported subscriber churn rose from 3.1% to 4.4%. Leadership wants a recommendation before next quarter's product roadmap is finalized.

responseCycle.prompt: Frame the decision and identify what must be clarified before diagnosing the churn increase.

criteria.label: Recognizes that the churn measure must be defined
Makes customer or product scope explicit
Connects the work to the roadmap deadline

comparison.title: One decision-ready opening
comparison.text: I want to establish which subscribers and churn definition drive the reported increase, then identify the product actions that can materially improve retention before the next roadmap is locked.

questionOptions.label: Is 4.4% monthly voluntary churn, and is the definition unchanged?
questionOptions.response: Yes. It is monthly voluntary churn, measured consistently with the prior period.

questionOptions.label: Which plans, tenures, or acquisition cohorts account for the increase?
questionOptions.response: The increase is concentrated among monthly-plan subscribers acquired through a recent promotional channel.

questionOptions.label: Which roadmap decisions are still reversible next quarter?
questionOptions.response: Onboarding and retention features can still be reprioritized; pricing changes require a later approval cycle.

questionOptions.label: Where is StreamWave's product team seated?
questionOptions.response: Team location does not affect the churn diagnosis.

questionOptions.label: Can we first document every competitor feature launched in five years?
questionOptions.response: Leadership needs a focused recommendation before that broad review could be completed.
